analysis: What changed vs the 7:00 AM brief: the selloff held its shape rather than deepening — Nasdaq -1.3%, S&P -0.4%, Dow -0.4% mid-morning versus -1.32%/-0.53%/-0.65% at the open. Within that steady tape, the rotation sharpened: Microsoft faded further (slightly negative at the open to -1.4% to -2% mid-morning) despite the beat and a 49% Q2 Azure growth expectation, ServiceNow deepened to about -26%, and Salesforce joined the software slide at -5%+. Offsetting that, DoorDash strengthened from +2% to +6% on the Instacart deal, Caterpillar eased off its worst, and Apple (+1.5%) and Meta (+2.2%) now lead the megacap divergence with Tesla slightly green. New context this hour: Alphabet's EPS miss partly reflects an unrealized SpaceX investment loss, which separates the noncash charge from the operating story — but the cash-burn and search-miss legs are what the tape is actually pricing. Signal: the market is still grading on cash conversion, guidance, and segment detail, and even winners are not immune in-session. Noise: the Marvell/Lumentum talks remain a single Bloomberg report with no company comment, and the Vance/Iran letter remains a reported overture. Carried forward: the ECB hold (deposit 2.50%) and Lagarde's Feb 7, 2027 departure, plus Q3 GDP 3.4% and core PCE 3.1% y/y, still frame the session — strong growth plus as-expected hot inflation, no relief for rate-sensitive tech.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Selloff holding, not deepening, mid-morning: Nasdaq Composite -1.3%, S&P 500 -0.4%, Dow -0.4%, Nasdaq 100 -1.3% — essentially the same shape as the open, with tech leading lower.
headlines.why_it_matters: Ninety minutes in, the tape has neither faded the Alphabet shock nor cascaded — the open's read is holding, so the after-close reports are now the next swing factor.

headlines.headline: Alphabet still down about 12% mid-morning (Finnhub: -12.45% to ~$284.43, from a $324.89 close): Q3 revenue $127.58B vs ~$128.22B expected, EPS $2.12 vs ~$3.02 expected — the EPS shortfall partly reflecting an unrealized investment loss tied to SpaceX — search ads $63.35B vs $64.96B expected, -$9.07B free cash flow on $51.4B quarterly capex, with 2027 capex set to rise significantly. Cloud still doubled (+103% to $30.7B).
headlines.why_it_matters: The decline has stuck through the morning — the market is pricing the cash-burn plus ads-miss combination as a re-rating, not a premarket overreaction.

headlines.headline: Microsoft's fade deepens: down 1.4% per Investopedia's mid-morning read (Finnhub: -2.03% to $520.22), from slightly negative at the open and +1.5% premarket, despite the fiscal Q1 beat (revenue $92.3B, Azure +48%, $18.6B free cash flow despite $45.2B capex) and a CFO expectation of 49% Azure growth in Q2.
headlines.why_it_matters: The winner from last night is now clearly red — in this tape even cash-backed beats are being pulled into the AI-spending risk-off move.

headlines.headline: Amazon down more than 3% mid-morning (Finnhub: -3.46% to ~$245.80) ahead of its after-close Q3 report (consensus EPS ~$1.97 per premarket briefing); Intel also reports after the close. MAGS ETF almost 2% lower.
headlines.why_it_matters: Amazon is being sold ahead of its own numbers on the same AI-capex question that hit Alphabet — tonight's AWS growth and spending guide are the next stock-specific test.

headlines.headline: Megacap divergence widens mid-morning: Apple +1.49% to $348.96, Meta +2.18% to $625.87, Tesla +0.25% to $405.24, while Nvidia slips -0.81% to $213.63 — against Alphabet -12% and Microsoft now red.
headlines.why_it_matters: Not a uniform megacap selloff — the pressure is concentrated in Alphabet-led AI-spending names, while Apple and Meta are being treated as separate stories.

headlines.headline: Software and chips keep sliding: ServiceNow plunges further to -25.75% ($111.47) after a small Q3 profit miss, Salesforce -5.27% in morning trading, Fortinet still near -26% despite a beat on slowing product-revenue growth. SOXX -2%, memory ETF DRAM -3%+ after jumping 7% yesterday; Samsung -4% in Seoul trading. Marvell -13% on the reported Lumentum deal talks; Lumentum +1.4%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The earnings-grading theme now spans chips and software alike — beats are being sold on growth detail, and the Marvell leg is single-source, unconfirmed — treat the deal leg as fragile.

headlines.headline: Offsets strengthen outside tech: DoorDash gains 6% on the $17B Instacart deal (up from +nearly 2% at the open); Caterpillar eases to -7.31% (from about -8% at the open) despite the Q3 beat, with guidance only maintained. Eli Lilly +more than 6%, Merck +5%, Chipotle +almost 7%, eBay +4%, Shell +2.6%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Healthcare and the DoorDash deal are cushioning the indexes — the Dow's drop is a Caterpillar story, not a broad blue-chip collapse, and the deal is gaining acceptance through the morning.

headlines.headline: Macro steady mid-morning: 10-year Treasury yield around 4.98%, unchanged from the 7 AM brief; WTI -2.2% to $100.47 on the reported Vance/Iran letter; Brent -1.9% to $109.56; gold -0.4% to $4,035; bitcoin near $80,000; December Fed-hike odds ~84% per CME FedWatch.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rates are not adding fresh pressure this morning — the selloff is an earnings story, not a rates story, with oil's pullback tied to a reported diplomatic overture, not a confirmed deal.
